newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Shell says to resume all Nigerian oil flow Monday.
newsitem.headline: Shell says to resume all Nigerian oil flow Monday.

text.p: The Nigerian unit of Royal Dutch Shell Group said on Monday it would resume oil output from its western sector which was disrupted last week.
"We intend to restart production today at Egwa, Jones Creek and Odidi areas," a company spokesman said in Lagos.
He said output had started at all five oil flow stations in Nembe creek in the southeast, which were also shut down on March 22 by a political dispute between villagers and the military government.
"Nembe production is back to normal. Three flow stations had restarted by Saturday, two yesterday and by midday production was back to normal," he said.
He added that "except for minor problems like terminal capacity the situation is now alright."
The spokesman said there was no new information on whether or not the threat of imposing a force majuere on Nigerian crude oil shipments had been lifted.

Militant villagers protesting against a merger of two communities and relocation of the capital of another council area last week disrupted Shell's operations in both the west and the east of the Niger delat, shutting in a total of 210,000 barrels per day (bpd) of crude oil.
The Shell spokesman said peace had been fully restored in the oil producing areas.
Nigerian oil communities have long been restive over the lack of modern amenities in their vicinities and frequently vent their anger by disrupting oil production activities.
